text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed sharply lower following a weaker New York market. May lost $31 to close at $1,610 per tonne, while July gave up $39 to close at $1,620 per tonne. The market showed little reaction to news a strike by stevedores continued to halt loadings at Brazil's key Santos port as coffee volume coming out of Brazil is not substantial at this time of the year. The strike, which paralyzed most loading operations except for a few vessels is expected to continue through Saturday. It is set to spread to the national level on Friday. Arabica futures in New York nosedived after defying an early call of 4 to 6 cents/lb better.

May lost 15.45 cents/lb to close at 177.70 cents/lb, while July lost 11.90 cents/lb to close at 163.35 cents/lb. Factors cited for the plunge include fund liquidation, options related selling and rumours of a possible build in US stocks in March by as much as 1 mn bags as a result of recent heavy shipments by producers. Even though it seems likely that Green Coffee Association stocks will be up sharply, the 1 mn bag figure seems a bit far fetched, some traders said. Shipments are expected to remain heavy up to the end of April. However, it is believed that any build in stocks in March and possibly April is likely to disappear in the second half of the year when shipments trail off substantially.

GUATEMALA - According to the president of the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) coffee exports in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 3.7 mn 60-kg bags, far above earlier expectations of 3 mn bags and up from the 3.6 mn bags exported in 1995/96. At the beginning of February Anacafe predicted production in 1996/97 to reach 3.0 mn bags, down from 3.6 mn bags produced the previous year, which is at odds with the latest export figure for 1996/97. Either production was higher than had been indicated or coffee has come in from other countries. Contraband coffee is well known to flow in the Mexico and Central American region, disturbing production and export figures. Different local tax regimes in the countries are blamed for the illegal trade.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 1.426 mn bags of coffee in January 1997, sharply up from the 746,035 bags exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (April) up to 14.295 mn bags, 18 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995/96. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 reached 13.7 mn bags, down from 15.8 mn bags the previous year. Main countries of destination for green coffee in April/ January 1996/97 were Germany (1.71 vs 0.687 mn bags), Italy (1.243 vs 1.207 mn bags), the United States (2.015 vs 1.665 mn bags) and Japan (1.057 vs 0.823 mn bags).

FINLAND - Finland imported 1.120 mn bags of coffee in 1996, 48 per cent more than was imported the previous year. The main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Kenya (102,900 vs 64,200 bags), Costa Rica (118,900 vs 98,100 bags), Guatemala (145,000 vs 85,900 bags), Brazil (204,300 vs 137,900 bags) and Colombia (260,000 vs 212,100 bags).
